sections.html:
Nobody else in Virginia is bigger. Virginia Beach counted 459,470 residents in 2020 and is estimated at 453,737 for 2025. It faces the Atlantic where the Chesapeake Bay opens up, roughly 19 miles from Norfolk and 107 miles from Richmond.

A line locals call the Green Line splits the built-up north from the farmland in the south. Open ground north of it is nearly gone, so buyers spend more time on resale homes and teardown or redevelopment lots.

Today's city took shape in 1963 as Princess Anne County folded together with the small resort town of Virginia Beach. One mailing address can mean an oceanfront block, a tract subdivision or a working farm. Sandbridge, Kempsville, Thalia, Great Neck Point, Bayside, Oceana, Pungo and Green Run all have their own pull. Say your community name first when you talk to anyone about the house, since ten minutes of driving can swap one set of buyers for another.

Low elevation and water on several sides make flooding the biggest environmental worry for many local homes. Hurricane Matthew put more than 2,000 houses underwater and left some streets flooded for days. Afterward the city refused several floodplain projects, and the developers lost their court challenges.

Prepare these before a buyer asks:

  • A quote from your insurer on flood coverage for your parcel.
  • Elevation certificates, repair invoices and past insurance claims.
  • A plain list of any time water got inside, repaired or not.

Disclose water history to a cash buyer at the start. An investor can subtract repair costs and still close. A retail buyer who finds the problem during inspection often just leaves.

sections.h2: Real estate tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Real estate bills come from the City Treasurer, who also collects them, in two payments per year. Should the date land on a Saturday, Sunday or city holiday, you have until the following business day.

PaymentDue dateCost of paying late
First installmentDecember 510% penalty or $10, whichever is greater, plus 9.6% interest a year
Second installmentJune 510% penalty or $10, whichever is greater, plus 9.6% interest a year

Each bill covers the city's fiscal year, which starts July 1 and ends June 30, and you pay it after that stretch of time is underway, not before. Homeowners whose lender pays from escrow should notify the Treasurer once the mortgage is paid off, because the bill otherwise keeps going to the lender.

Names on the ownership rolls at the Real Estate Assessor's Office change when a new deed reaches the Circuit Court clerk. More detail is on the Virginia Beach Treasurer's real estate page .

sections.h2: Splitting the tax bill at closing
sections.html:
On the settlement statement, the year's full tax is divided by days. You cover the days you held title and the buyer covers the remainder of the fiscal year. Your closing agent does the math.

Any delinquent balance gets collected before a refund is released, so deal with old debt first. If you owe back taxes, phone the Treasurer's office early and request a payoff amount good for your closing date. That number is much easier to get a week out than on settlement morning.

Recording a deed triggers two state charges of its own. One is the recordation tax, 25 cents per $100 (section 58.1-801 ). The other is the grantor's tax, 50 cents per $500 (section 58.1-802 ), which the seller carries unless the buyer agrees to pay it.

Page one of the deed has to show the sale price before the clerk will accept it.

The state's disclosure statute for home sellers does not reach every transfer. Executors and other fiduciaries running an estate, guardianship, conservatorship or trust are outside it, as listed in section 55.1-702 .

Foreclosure transfers and gifts between spouses or direct family are outside it as well. An estate attorney can tell you where yours lands. Round up the death certificate, the court order naming the personal representative and the deed so buyers are not left waiting on paper.

sections.h2: Military moves and fixed closing dates
sections.html:
The bases drive much of the local economy, and NAS Oceana is the largest single employer. Service members with new orders may have to be gone by a date set for them, whether a transfer or a deployment. A sure closing day then beats squeezing out a bit more price.

Give your deadline on the first call. Have each buyer name a closing day in writing, along with anything that could delay it, like a loan or an appraisal.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale a fit for you?
sections.html:
Often. Flood damage, postponed repairs, tenants or a military move can stall a normal listing. Without a lender, the deal does not wait on a loan decision or a bank appraiser.

The path is short. An offer arrives in writing. A title company searches for liens against the deed. At closing, back taxes and any mortgage balance come out of the proceeds, and the deed is sent to the circuit court. You choose the closing day, within what the title work allows.

Compare each offer with what a listing could realistically bring. Subtract repairs, carrying costs and taxes from the written number to see your take-home. Keep your latest tax bill, mortgage statement and repair records beside you for the first call.

No showings, no open houses and no round of buyer repair requests either. For an empty house, an inherited one or a rental with tenants, that can spare you months of upkeep and another tax installment.

sections.h2: What to bring to a first conversation
sections.html:
A short stack of papers speeds everything up: the deed or a recent tax bill showing the parcel, your mortgage statement with a payoff phone number, any flood insurance paperwork, and receipts for work done on the house.

If tenants live there, add the lease. If the owner has died, add the estate papers. A buyer who sees these items on day one can usually put a number on the house within a few days instead of weeks. Ask each buyer what they would need from you before closing, and answer in writing so the terms stay clear.

sections.h2: What to do if you owe taxes
sections.html:
Owing back real estate tax will not block a sale. The balance is settled out of your proceeds, with the title company requesting the exact payoff, penalty and interest included, from the Treasurer. If you want choices before the next due date, ask the Treasurer's office now, because the 10% penalty starts the moment a payment is late.

For someone watching a balance grow, a cash sale ends it at the closing table, and whatever is left comes to you.

faqs.q: When are Virginia Beach real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Bills come in two installments, due December 5 and June 5. A weekend or holiday due date moves to the next business day.

faqs.q: How are taxes prorated when a Virginia Beach house sells?
faqs.a: The full annual tax for the fiscal year is divided by days. Your closing agent puts that split on the settlement statement.

faqs.q: Can I sell a flood-damaged Virginia Beach house?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers shy away from flood damage, but a direct cash buyer can price the repairs in and buy as is. Gather any insurance claims and repair records first.

faqs.q: How many boroughs does Virginia Beach have?
faqs.a: Seven: Bayside, Blackwater, Kempsville, Lynnhaven, Princess Anne, Pungo and Virginia Beach. They date from the 1963 merger of Princess Anne County and the city.

faqs.q: Who pays the grantor's tax on a Virginia Beach sale?
faqs.a: The seller, unless the buyer agrees to take it on. The rate is 50 cents per $500 under Virginia Code 58.1-802.
